speaker: Other
text: Thanks for joining. I am Mara from Larkspur Health, I lead the claims platform team.

speaker: Alex
text: Happy to be here. I am Dana, I work on backend and machine learning systems.

speaker: Other
text: Could you start with a short summary of your background?

speaker: Alex
text: Six years in production systems. First payments at Northwind Freight, then a claims-triage model at a health company.

speaker: Other
text: Tell me about Harbor Ledger. What was your role there?

speaker: Alex
text: I designed it and led it. It reconciled about 41,000 payments a month and cut the month-end close from six days to two.

speaker: Other
text: What was the hardest part of that project?

speaker: Alex
text: Duplicate postings. In March 2021 a nightly job posted 300 payments twice because an idempotency key was missing.

speaker: Other
text: How did you find it?

speaker: Alex
text: A reconciliation alert fired at six in the morning. I traced it to the retry path within one hour.

speaker: Other
text: And what did you change afterwards?

speaker: Alex
text: I wrote a replay-safe fix the same day and added a reconciliation check that has caught every duplicate since.

speaker: Other
text: Good. Let us talk about the team. How many people would you work with?

speaker: Alex
text: I would like to understand that from you. What does the team look like today?

speaker: Other
text: Seven engineers, two data scientists and one product manager. We are hiring two more.

speaker: Alex
text: That sounds like a good size. Who owns the serving stack?

speaker: Other
text: The platform team owns serving. The data scientists own the models, and you would sit between them.

speaker: Alex
text: I have done that before at Northwind, between finance engineers and the payments team.

speaker: Other
text: What is your experience with Kafka?

speaker: Alex
text: Three years. Harbor Ledger consumed payment events from Kafka and I tuned partitions and consumer lag alerts.

speaker: Other
text: Do you have experience with model monitoring?

speaker: Alex
text: Some. I built drift checks for the claims-triage model, but I have not run a full monitoring platform.

speaker: Other
text: That is honest. We would need someone to grow into that.

speaker: Alex
text: I would be glad to. I say what I tested and what I did not test, so I would start with the gaps.

speaker: Other
text: Let us talk about timing. When could you start?

speaker: Alex
text: From January 2027. I am finishing a project until the end of December.

speaker: Other
text: Remote or Lisbon?

speaker: Alex
text: Either. Lisbon is my base, but remote in Europe works too.

speaker: Other
text: What salary range are you looking for?

speaker: Alex
text: I would like to hear the range for this level first, then we can see if it fits.

speaker: Other
text: The range is between 85,000 and 100,000 euros gross per year.

speaker: Alex
text: That is inside what I had in mind. I will confirm after the next conversation.

speaker: Other
text: Next step is a technical interview with two of my engineers.

speaker: Alex
text: Great. Should I prepare anything specific?

speaker: Other
text: A short design discussion about a batch scoring service. No homework.

speaker: Alex
text: Understood. I will send my availability by Friday.

speaker: Other
text: One more question. What do you do when a number in a report looks wrong?

speaker: Alex
text: I check the source first, then the transformation, and I tell the reader what I could not verify.

speaker: Other
text: Thank you Dana. We will be in touch this week.

speaker: Alex
text: Thank you Mara. Talk soon.
